title: Çatalca — pine edge and hazel coppice
description: Field finds, photo IDs and the chemistry behind them. Shelf 3: Çatalca, pine edge and hazel coppice, 22 Nov 2026.
lede: A late-afternoon walk that crossed from pine into an old hazel coppice. The pine side had been raked over by kanlıca pickers; the hazel side had not, and it held three death caps, a white Amanita and a crowd of clouded agarics in one small patch. Brackets were sampled for the lab; nothing was eaten. Spore prints and underside photos follow.

finds.name: Foliose lichen
finds.id: Grey-green leafy lobes on a cut pine stump.
finds.chem: Usnic-acid family, antimicrobial; lichens are air-quality indicators.
finds.check: A lichen is a fungus living with an alga, not a mushroom.

finds.name: Zoned bracket, coin-size
finds.id: Small zoned bracket on a pine stump; pale cream underside with rusty-red spots at the base (second photo).
finds.chem: Trametes: PSK/PSP beta-glucans (hot-water extract). Stereum: nothing of interest.
finds.check: Pin-hole pores (3–5 per mm) = Trametes. Smooth suede that bleeds red on a scratch = Stereum sanguinolentum.

finds.name: Clouded agaric or grey knight troop
finds.id: A troop of grey caps in pine litter.
finds.check: Sweet-rancid smell + cream gills running down the stem = nebularis. Pink spore print = Entoloma, toxic.

finds.name: Bonnets
finds.id: Small grey bell caps on thin stems in pine litter.
finds.chem: A few Mycena carry muscarine; only M. cyanorrhiza is reported to hold trace psilocybin.
finds.check: White or grey gills + white print + radish smell = Mycena. No bluing.

finds.name: Funnel cap or faded blewit
finds.id: Pale funnel-shaped cap in hazel litter.

finds.name: Death cap, young
finds.id: Young olive-tinged cap in broadleaf litter; volva not dug out.
finds.chem: Amatoxins, RNA-polymerase II inhibitors; liver failure after a 6–24 h symptom-free gap.

finds.name: Hazel coppice path
finds.id: The hazel coppice side of the walk: old stools, cut and regrown.

finds.name: White fans on bark
finds.id: Small white fan-shaped caps on bark.
finds.chem: Schizophyllum: schizophyllan (sizofiran), a beta-glucan; the easiest wood-rotter to culture.

finds.name: Oysterling
finds.id: Small shell-shaped caps on a fallen hazel stick.
finds.check: Plain gills going brown = Crepidotus. Wrinkled veins = Plicatura.

finds.name: Clouded agaric
finds.id: Grey-brown caps, cream decurrent gills; the second photo (14:42) is the cluster at the hazel stools.
finds.chem: Nebularine; stomach upset in a good share of eaters.
finds.check: Look for Volvariella surrecta riding an old cap.

finds.name: Hairy curtain crust
finds.id: Hairy zoned bracket; confirmed by the orange smooth underside.
finds.chem: No pores, no PSK; the standard turkey-tail double.

finds.name: The deceiver
finds.id: Small tan caps with thick pinkish widely-spaced gills, hazel litter.
finds.chem: Mycorrhizal with hazel, so not culturable like a wood-rotter.
finds.check: Thick pinkish widely-spaced gills + white print = Laccaria. Rusty gills or a cobweb veil = Cortinarius (kidney risk).

finds.name: Hazelnut
finds.id: A hazelnut in the soil; confirms the coppice is hazel.

finds.name: Fibrous tan cap on buried wood
finds.flagText: Treat as Amanita until the base is dug out
finds.id: Called Pluteus in the field; may well be another Amanita.
finds.chem: P. salicinus is the one European Pluteus with psilocybin.
finds.check: Free gills going pink + no volva = Pluteus. Any sac at the base = Amanita, stop.

finds.name: Death cap
finds.id: Textbook: white sac volva visible at the base.
finds.chem: Amatoxins, RNA-polymerase II inhibitors; liver failure after a 6–24 h symptom-free gap.

finds.name: Death cap, mature
finds.id: Flat cap, torn ring on the stem.
finds.chem: Amatoxins, RNA-polymerase II inhibitors; liver failure after a 6–24 h symptom-free gap.

finds.name: Turkey tail or hairy bracket
finds.id: Rosettes on a dead hazel stem; sampled and taken home.
finds.chem: PSK/PSP beta-glucans (hot-water extract); T. hirsuta laccase.
finds.lab: Underside photo in daylight, then dry for a hot-water extract; the stem chunk is the culture source.

finds.name: Brittlegill
finds.id: Purple-red cap in pine needles.

finds.name: False chanterelle
finds.id: Orange cap with forking gills in pine litter.
finds.check: Forking orange gills. Orange milk going green = Lactarius deliciosus instead.

finds.name: Destroying angel
finds.id: Two fruitbodies at the pine edge. Pure white cap and gills, ring on the stem, bulb with a sac; the second has a shaggy stem and a torn veil at the foot.
